'''Deni Avdija''' ({{lang-he|דני אבדיה}}, {{lang-sr-cyr|Дени Авдија}}; born 3 January 2001) is an Israeli-Serbian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Listed at 2.06 m (6 ft 9 in), he plays the [[small forward]] and [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. He is projected as a top 5 pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]].  

The son of basketball player [[Zufer Avdija]], he joined Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2013 and excelled as a youth player. He debuted for their senior team in 2017, at age 16, becoming the youngest in club history. Two years later, he became the youngest player to ever win the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli League Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) award and led his team to the Israeli League championship.

Avdija is also a member of the [[Israel national basketball team|Israeli senior national team]]. He has won two [[gold medal]]s for Israel at the youth level, including at the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship]], where he was named tournament MVP.

==Early life and youth career==
Avdija was born on kibbutz [[Beit Zera]], Israel.<ref name="maccabi">{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija |url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/player.asp?PlayerID=955&cYear=2020&lang=en |publisher=[[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] |accessdate=11 April 2020}}</ref> He played [[association football]] until he entered fourth grade, when he began focusing on [[basketball]], the sport his father played professionally.<ref name="sachs">{{cite web |last1=Sachs |first1=Frankie |title=Conversation with Deni Avdija, Maccabi |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/a4w8t8pomc8mgpwm/conversation-with-deni-avdija-maccabi |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=23 October 2019}}</ref> Avdija initially competed at the youth level for [[Bnei Herzliya]], and in 2013, he joined the youth ranks of [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] where he played under the coach Shai Omer.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=מניה בצמיחה / דני אבדיה הוא הדבר הבא|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5311930,00.html|publisher=[[Ynet]]|access-date=21 July 2018|date=18 July 2018|language=he}}</ref> From 2017 to 2019, Avdija led Maccabi Tel Aviv to three consecutive Israeli youth state championships.<ref>{{Cite web|title=בפעם הרביעית ברציפות: קבוצת הנוער של מכבי ת"א זכתה באליפות|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5517407,00.html|publisher= [[Ynet]] |access-date=31 May 2019|date=29 May 2019|language=he}}</ref> In August 2018, he participated in [[Basketball Without Borders]] Europe in [[Belgrade]], where he was named camp MVP.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jokic, Vucevic Headline Basketball Without Borders Europe 2018 |url=http://global.nba.com/news/jokic-vucevic-headline-basketball-without-borders-europe-2018/ |publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | date=14 August 2018 |accessdate=18 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Djordjevic |first1=Stefan |title=Deni Avdija named Basketball Without Borders MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/726859/deni-avdija-named-basketball-without-borders-mvp/ |publisher=EuroHoops| date=18 August 2018 | accessdate=18 August 2018}}</ref>

In January 2019, Avdija played for Maccabi Tel Aviv's U18 team at [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT) in [[Munich]]. He was selected to the all-tournament team after leading the event with 24.3 [[point (basketball)|points]], 6 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 3.8 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and a [[Performance Index Rating]] (PIR) of 31.5. Avdija also ranked second among all players with 11 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, while helping his team finish in second place.<ref name="hein">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Maccabi's Avdija is just #LivingTheDream |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9felb3mwhqcicmyh/maccabi-s-avdija-is-just-livingthedream |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=28 January 2019}}</ref> In February, at [[2019 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], Avdija was named MVP of the Basketball Without Borders Global Camp.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gay |first1=Carlan | title=Deni Avdija, Aaliyah Mckenzie Edwards take home MVP at Basketball Without Borders Global 2019 | url=https://ca.nba.com/news/deni-avdija-aaliyah-mckenzie-edwards-mvp-at-bwb-gloabl-2019-recap/oxb4bvwlgnx01o3xb5eakhvtm | website=[[NBA.com]] | accessdate=18 February 2019 | date=18 February 2019}}</ref> In May, he joined Maccabi Tel Aviv's U18 team for the [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Final Tournament|ANGT Finals]]. He collected all-tournament team honours after leading the event with 24.7 points and 12 rebounds per game with a PIR of 29.7, while ranking second with 6.7 assists per game.<ref name="angtfinals">{{cite web |title=MVP Nakic of Real Madrid headlines All-Tournament Team |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9occvq9c8tn4qe63/mvp-nakic-of-real-madrid-headlines-all-tournament-team |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=19 May 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2017–present)===
On 5 November 2017, Avdija started his professional career with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], signing a six-year deal with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv signs prospect Deni Avdija to a six-year contract|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/252732/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-prospect-deni-avdija-to-a-six-year-contract.html|publisher=Sportando|access-date=21 July 2018|date=5 November 2017}}</ref> On 19 November, he made his professional debut in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]], playing three minutes against [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]]. At 16 years and 320 days of age, he became the youngest player to ever play for his club's senior team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winner League, Game 7: Nes Ziona Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23190&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|access-date=21 July 2018|date=19 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=חי את החלום – דני אבדיה בראיון|url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/magazines/newsPage.asp?newsID=981|publisher=[[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]|access-date=2 November 2019|date=7 February 2019|language=he}}</ref> Avdija made his [[EuroLeague]] debut on 22 November 2018, at the age of 17, in a 74–70 loss to [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]]. He scored two points in three minutes of playing time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=67&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. Fenerbahce BEKO Istanbul – Game|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|access-date=12 February 2020|date=22 November 2018}}</ref>
[[File:Deni Avdija vs Milano (cropped).jpg|thumb|Avdija (left) attempts a [[Three-point field goal|three-pointer]] over [[Olimpia Milano]]'s [[Vladimir Micov]] in November 2019.]]
On 24 October 2019, at the age of 18, Avdija made his first start in the EuroLeague, recording six points and three rebounds in 16 minutes in a 76–63 victory over [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=67&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. Valencia Basket – Game|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|access-date=26 October 2019|date=24 October 2019}}</ref> On 11 January 2020, Avdija recorded a then career-high of 22 points, shooting 9-of-15 from the field, and five assists in a 94–83 win over [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winner League, Game 15: U-NET Holon Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24109&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|access-date=11 January 2020|date=11 January 2020}}</ref> On 31 January 2020, Avdija was named [[2019–20 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Israeli Player of the Month|Israeli Player of the Month]] in the Israeli League after averaging 14.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, with an 18.3 PIR, in four games played that month.<ref>{{cite news|title=שחקן החודש הישראלי: דני אבדיה|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=23112|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|date=31 January 2020|access-date=31 January 2020|language=he}}</ref> On 1 February 2020, Avdija established a new career-high of 26 points, shooting 9-of-12 from the field, and grabbed six rebounds in an 86–81 loss to [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 18: Hapoel Yossi Avrahami Eilat Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24125&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|date=1 February 2020|access-date=1 February 2020}}</ref> Six days later, he scored 13 points, including eight in the second quarter, in a 78–77 victory over Fenerbahçe.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hunter lifts Maccabi at finish over Fenerbahce |url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=213&seasoncode=E2019#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=19 July 2020 |date=7 February 2020}}</ref> His dunk over [[Luigi Datome]] during the game would be named [[EuroLeague Magic Moment of the Season]] in July 2020.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=EuroLeague |author=EuroLeague |number=1284877355534737408 |date = 19 July 2020 |title=Here it is... The @7DAYSBasketball Magic Moment of the 2019/20 season The Deni Avdija Poster Jam}}</ref> On 16 April, Avdija declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Potential top-five pick Deni Avdija seeks entry to 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29043324/potential-top-five-pick-deni-avdija-seeks-entry-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=17 April 2020 |date=16 April 2020}}</ref> 

Avdija's season was suspended for about three months due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. He returned to action on 21 June, recording 23 points, seven rebounds and five assists in 24 minutes in a 114–82 win over [[Maccabi Ashdod B.C.|Maccabi Ashdod]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija erupts with 23 points in Israeli League’s return |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1072537/deni-avdija-erupts-with-23-points-in-israeli-leagues-return/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=21 June 2020 |date=21 June 2020}}</ref> On 23 July, he scored 22 points, including 10 in the fourth quarter, and grabbed 10 rebounds in an 83–68 win over [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]], helping Maccabi Tel Aviv advance to the Israeli League Final Four.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dorsey, Avdija step up and lift shorthanded Maccabi over Hapoel to win the series |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1083800/dorsey-avdija-step-up-and-lift-shorthanded-maccabi-over-hapoel-to-win-the-series/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=23 July 2020 |date=23 July 2020}}</ref> In the Final on 28 July, Avdija recorded five points, seven rebounds, four assists and two steals to help Maccabi Tel Aviv defeat [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]], 86–81.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Deni Avdija plays last game in Europe, wins championship |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1085242/deni-avdija-plays-last-game-in-europe-wins-championship/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=28 July 2020 |date=28 July 2020}}</ref> He became the youngest player to ever win the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli League MVP]] award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola |title=Deni Avdija named Israeli league MVP, youngest to win award in league history |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/deni-avdija-named-israeli-league-mvp-youngest-to-win-award-in-league-history/ |publisher=Sportando |accessdate=28 July 2020 |date=28 July 2020}}</ref> Avdija was also named Israeli League Israeli Player of the Year and was an [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Quintet|All-Israeli League First Team]] selection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija named Winner League’s Israeli Player of the Year |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1084675/deni-avdija-named-winner-leagues-israeli-player-of-the-year/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=28 July 2020 |date=26 July 2020}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 12.9 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game in the Israeli League. In the EuroLeague, Avdija averaged four points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 14.3 minutes per game.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Deni-Avdija/Summary/116938 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=9 August 2020}}</ref>

Avdija is training in [[Atlanta]] for the NBA draft.

==National team career==
===Junior team===
[[File:Deni Avdija.jpg|thumb|left|Avdija shoots a [[free throw]] for [[Israel national under-18 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] in April 2018.]]
Although he had also been eligible to represent [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbia]] internationally, due to his father's background, Avdija chose to play for [[Israel national basketball team|Israel]] because he had friends there and was more familiar with its language.<ref name=zadar>{{cite web |last1=Wawrzyńczuk |first1=Bronisław |title=Zadar Basketball Tournament Interview: Deni Avdija |url=https://eurospects.com/?p=14463 |publisher=Eurospects |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=25 September 2018}}</ref> He competed for [[Israel men's national under-16 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]]. Avdija led the tournament with 12.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, to go with 15.3 points per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Avdija in the 2017 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/player/Deni-Avdija|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=19 August 2017|accessdate=22 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2017 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship Players Statistics |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/playerstats |website=fiba.basketball |accessdate=8 March 2019}}</ref>

In April 2018, Avdija averaged over 17 points and nine rebounds for [[Israel national under-18 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], an under-18 competition in [[Mannheim]].<ref name="halickman">{{cite web |last1=Halickman |first1=Joshua |title=Latest Israeli hoops protégé Deni Avdija finding his wings |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/latest-israeli-hoops-prot%C3%A9g%C3%A9-deni-avdija-finding-his-wings-562999 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=20 July 2018}}</ref> In July 2018, he played at the [[2018 FIBA U20 European Championship|FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Chemnitz]], leading [[Israel national under-20 basketball team|Israel]] to a gold medal. Avdija averaged 12.7 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.3 steals per game, while earning a spot on the [[2018 FIBA U20 European Championship#All-Tournament Team|all-tournament team]] with teammate [[Yovel Zoosman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2018/news/israel-swingman-zoosman-snatches-up-mvp-honors|title=Israel swingman Zoosman snatches up MVP honors|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=22 July 2018|accessdate=22 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Avdija in the 2018 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2018/player/Deni-Avdija|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=22 July 2018|accessdate=22 July 2018}}</ref> Later that month, Avdija competed at the [[2018 FIBA U18 European Championship Division B|FIBA U18 European Championship Division B]] in [[Skopje]]. Appearing tired from his previous tournament and lacking in endurance, he averaged 17.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3 assists and 1.4 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=FIBA U18 Division B – Top Performers |url=http://www.eurohopes.com/news/6263/fiba_u18_division_b_-_top_performers |publisher=Eurohopes |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=10 December 2018}}</ref>

In July 2019, Avdija led Israel to a second straight gold medal at the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship|FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Tel Aviv]]. He averaged 18.4 points, 8.3 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 2.4 blocks and 2.1 steals per game, earning MVP and all-tournament team accolades, as the second-youngest player at the event.<ref name="obsession">{{cite web |title=In Deni Avdija's world, basketball is a 24/7 obsession |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2019/news/in-deni-avdija-s-world-basketball-is-a-24/7-obsession |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=20 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija completes MVP tournament with strong showing |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/910377/deni-avdija-completes-mvp-tournament-with-strong-showing/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=21 July 2019}}</ref> Avdija tallied 26 points, 11 rebounds and 5 steals against France in the semifinal, before recording 23 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds and 3 blocks against [[Spain national under-20 basketball team|Spain]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/909981/deni-avdija-puts-on-a-show-as-israel-moves-to-final/|title=Deni Avdija puts on a show as Israel moves to Final|publisher=EuroHoops|date=20 July 2019|accessdate=21 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/910346/avdija-powers-israel-to-the-top-of-u20-european-championship/|title=Avdija powers Israel to the top of U20 European Championship|publisher=EuroHoops|date=21 July 2019|accessdate=21 July 2019}}</ref>

===Senior team===
On 21 February 2019, Avdija made his debut for the [[Israel national basketball team|Israeli senior national team]], in an 81–77 win over [[Germany national basketball team|Germany]], during the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2019 FIBA World Cup qualification]] stage.<ref>{{cite web|title=Israel v Germany boxscore – FIBA Basketball World Cup 2019 European Qualifiers|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/european-qualifiers/game/2102/Israel-Germany|date=21 February 2019|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=21 February 2019}}</ref> On 24 February 2020, he recorded 21 points and eight rebounds in 24 minutes in an 87–63 victory over [[Romania national basketball team|Romania]] during the [[EuroBasket 2021 qualification|EuroBasket 2021 qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Avdija shines bright as Israel complete perfect first window |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2021/qualifiers/news/avdija-shines-bright-as-israel-complete-perfect-first-window |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=24 February 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father [[Zufer Avdija]] was born in [[Pristina]], [[SFR Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] (nowadays in Kosovo), and is a Serbian-Israeli citizen of [[Gorani people|Gorani]]-[[Muslim]] heritage.<ref name=maccabi/><ref name=obsession/><ref name="griver">{{cite web |last1=Griver |first1=Simon |title=Avdija tipped to be no. 1 in NBA draft |url=https://www.thejc.com/sport/sport-news/avdija-nba-basketball-1.498636 |website=[[The Jewish Chronicle]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=31 March 2020}}</ref> A professional basketball player in Yugoslavia and Israel, Zufer spent 11 years of his playing career with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and was the team's [[captain (sports)|captain]] in the 1980s, before moving to the [[Israeli Premier League]] in the 1990s and playing 8 seasons for [[Israel]]i clubs [[A.S. Ramat HaSharon|Ramat HaSharon]], [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Rishon LeZion]], [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]], and Elitzur [[Bat Yam]].<ref name=Bio/><ref name=obsession/><ref name="schmitz">{{cite web |last1=Schmitz |first1=Mike |title=Deni Avdija could be a polarizing top draft prospect in 2020 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27281239/deni-avdija-polarizing-top-draft-prospect-2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=29 July 2019}}</ref> He also represented the [[Yugoslavia national basketball team|Yugoslavian national team]] internationally, with whom he won the bronze medal at the [[1982 FIBA World Championship]].<ref name=sachs/> Avdija's mother, Sharon Artzi, an [[Israeli Jews|Israeli Jew]] from Kibbutz Beit Zera, is a former [[track and field]] athlete and basketball player.<ref name=maccabi/><ref name=sachs/><ref name=schmitz/><ref name="weitzman">{{cite web |last1=Weitzman |first1=Yaron |title='We've Never Had a Talent Like Him' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2861981-weve-never-had-a-talent-like-him |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=10 April 2020 |date=15 November 2019}}</ref>

Avdija holds [[Multiple citizenship|dual citizenship]] of Israel and [[Serbia]], the latter because his father is a Serbian citizen.<ref name=zadar/><ref>{{cite web |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv pens long-term deal with Deni Avdija |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/547778/maccabi-tel-aviv-pens-long-term-deal-deni-avdija/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=5 November 2017}}</ref> When he turned 18 years old, he received a deferment from mandatory service in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) due to his basketball career.<ref name=weitzman/> On 1 April 2020, while the basketball season was suspended as a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Avdija was drafted into the IDF for a short service.<ref name=halickman2>{{cite web |last1=Halickman |first1=Joshua |title=Israeli basketball phenom Deni Avdija drafted into IDF |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/israeli-basketball-phenom-deni-avdija-drafted-into-idf-623217 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |accessdate=11 April 2020 |date=1 April 2020}}</ref>
